learning_outcomes.text: The course introduces students to the study of electromagnetic wave propagation at optical frequencies, and to the analysis of optoelectronic and photonic components directly related to the teacher's experience in the field of European Project Design. Fundamental concepts on nanostructured materials (e.g. graphene, carbon nanotubes), their interaction with light, and related applications in optoelectronics and photonics are introduced.

Thanks to the tools of mathematical physics, and in light of recent discoveries in the field of nanotechnologies, students will develop the ability to design i) optical fiber and planar waveguide devices, ii) photodetectors and photovoltaic cells based on nanostructured materials, iii) rectennas (nanoantenna-diodes) for energy harvesting.

Within the Photonics and Nanotechnologies course, students must apply methods and notions learned in basic and characteristic courses, in order to carry out a multidisciplinary synthesis activity to evaluate project correspondence to requirements and to understand the advantages and limitations of different design alternatives.

syllabus_topics: Surface waves and THz amplification in 2D materials
Use of COMSOL Multi-physics in the numerical simulation of optoelectronic and photonic components
assessment_rules: The assessment of the learning level consists of an oral examination. For students with disabilities/invalidities or specific learning disorders (DSA) who have requested support from the university's Disability/DSA Info Point, the exam methods will be adapted according to university guidelines. Students must demonstrate mastery of the concepts introduced in the course, particularly being able to introduce, derive, argue, demonstrate, and connect relationships and theories related to the topics covered. The exam evaluates effort, acquired knowledge, comprehension, and analytical and critical skills. The final grade is a weighted evaluation of these measurement criteria.
